newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel proposes NTT interconnection rules.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel proposes NTT interconnection rules.

text.p: An advisory body to Japan's Posts and Telecommunications Minister on Thursday proposed connection rules aimed at requiring Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp to give rival phone firms fair access to its networks.

The recommendations, largely in line with preliminary guidelines announced in September, would set up an accounting system for calculating the cost of connecting rival phone firms to NTT's networks, in order to assure that the company charges appropriate interconnection rates.
The panel's proposals would also give other carriers the right to connect to all possible points in NTT's networks.

In a departure from the preliminary guidelines, however, the body did not set a date for implementing portability of telephone numbers, which would allow NTT customers who switch to rival carriers to keep their old phone numbers.
Legislation to implement the panel's recommendations is scheduled to be introduced in Japan's parliament next month.

The recommendations, which require all telecommunications carriers to give competitors access to their networks, included special accounting rules for NTT, which virtually monopolises local call networks.
